ai.title: Normalize placeholder comments and skip test billing
ai.summary: Added `replaceNonStandardPlaceholderComments` to normalize AI-generated placeholder comments into standard formats across multiple languages before patch generation. Introduced `TEST_USER_ID` constant and updated `promptOpenAI` to skip `saveMessage` billing tracking when the user ID matches this test constant. Changes affect `backend/src/generate-patch.ts`, `backend/src/openai-api.ts`, and `common/src/util/string.ts`.

eli5.text: When the assistant writes code edits, some placeholder comments it leaves behind (like "...rest unchanged...") now get cleaned up into a consistent standard format before the final patch is created, so generated files look tidy across languages like Python, Java, SQL, and HTML. Test runs on a special internal account no longer charge the company's pay-as-you-go billing as they generate sample responses. The cleanup runs automatically behind the scenes in the patch-making tool; you'd only notice if you regularly inspect the generated code comments or manage internal test usage.

ai.title: Replace console and debugLog with pino structured logging
ai.summary: Backend logging migrated to pino, replacing console.log, console.error, and custom debugLog calls across claude.ts, generate-knowledge-files.ts, generate-patch.ts, index.ts, main-prompt.ts, and openai-api.ts. Production uses JSON output, development uses pino-pretty transport, with levels controlled by LOG_LEVEL env var. Updates backend/knowledge.md documenting the new logging strategy and configuration.

eli5.text: The software behind the assistant used to print all its operational messages in a messy, informal format using basic console commands. Now, it uses a structured logging system that formats every message consistently, making it easier for the team to search, filter, and understand what the system is doing. If you looked at the system's technical documentation or logs today, you'd notice the messages follow a standard format and can be sorted by importance levels like error, warning, or info. This change affects how the team maintains and monitors the system, improving reliability and debugging.

ai.title: Replace logger with console in env config
ai.summary: Removed `logger` import and replaced `logger.info` with `console.log` in `backend/src/env.mjs`. This avoids using the application logger during early environment configuration, preventing potential circular dependencies or premature initialization issues. Scope limited to backend environment setup.

eli5.text: When the backend first starts up to read basic settings, it stopped writing startup messages through the main application logger and now uses the system's built-in console output instead. This prevents a startup ordering problem where the logging system might try to load before the settings it needs are ready, which could have caused confusing failures during environment initialization. Nothing you see as a user changes; the same message still appears, just printed differently behind the scenes while the server boots. This is internal housekeeping on the live system today.

ai.title: AsyncLocalStorage binds pino context to websocket actions
ai.summary: logger.ts wraps pino with AsyncLocalStorage via a mixin, exposing withLoggerContext to inject request-scoped fields. websocket-action.ts calls withLoggerContext around onUserInput, attaching fingerprintId, authToken, and clientRequestId to all downstream logs. Scope is backend logging and websocket handlers only. Context merges with existing store values, enabling correlated logs across async boundaries without manual parameter threading.

eli5.text: When you interact with the assistant over a WebSocket (the live connection used for real-time chat), every log message it produces now automatically includes three hidden identifiers: your fingerprint ID, auth token, and client request ID. This means that instead of seeing a single disconnected log line per event, you can trace an entire request from start to finish across all internal systems without any code changes. The logging system now uses a context-tracking mechanism behind the scenes that automatically attaches your session information to every log entry made during your interaction, so support engineers can quickly find and understand your specific session's logs without manually searching through unrelated entries.

ai.title: Consolidate backend logging calls
ai.summary: Refactors logging in `backend/src` to use structured `logger.debug`/`logger.info` calls with consistent object payloads. Removes verbose inline logs, redundant `console.error` usage, and unused imports like `fs`/`path` in `main-prompt.ts`. Updates `system-prompt.ts` to log detailed token counts from `getTruncatedFilesBasedOnTokenBudget` and removes the unused `getRelevantFilesPrompt` export. Scope limited to internal backend observability; no user-facing behavior changes.

eli5.text: The team cleaned up how the app writes to its internal logbooks. Instead of scattering short, inconsistent notes across multiple files, the backend now writes structured entries that bundle related details (like message counts, token usage, and file paths) into single, labeled records. You won't see anything new on your screen, but if you open the logs today, they are easier to scan and search.

ai.title: Consolidate requestRelevantFiles logs
ai.summary: Refactored `requestRelevantFiles` and `generateFileRequests` to consolidate multiple scattered `logger.info` calls into single structured log entries. `checkNewFilesNecessary` now returns an object containing both the boolean result and the raw response string for better traceability. `getRelevantFiles` returns the full result object including `requestType` and `response` instead of just files and duration. Updated `backend/src/request-files-prompt.ts`.

eli5.text: The system behind the assistant’s file-finding feature cleaned up how it records what it's doing. Instead of scattering small, separate log messages across multiple steps, it now bundles the relevant details into a few single, structured log entries, making the internal process easier for the team to read and trace. This is behind-the-scenes maintenance that doesn’t change how the assistant behaves day to day.

ai.title: Backend uncaughtException handler added
ai.summary: Added process.on('uncaughtException') to backend/src/index.ts. Logs fatal errors via logger.fatal, closes server, and exits with code 1. Includes 1-second timeout fallback to process.abort() if graceful shutdown fails. Internal change affecting backend error handling.

eli5.text: When something goes seriously wrong in the backend that it wasn't prepared for, the system will now catch that problem, log it as a critical error, shut down the server gracefully, and then stop the process. If the graceful shutdown takes too long, the process will force itself to stop immediately. This is a behind-the-scenes change to improve error handling and stability for the backend.

ai.title: Logger: pino level label and ISO timestamp
ai.summary: Updated backend logger config in `backend/src/util/logger.ts` to format log levels as uppercase strings and use ISO 8601 timestamps. Added `formatters.level` to convert pino's numeric level to its label, and a custom `timestamp` function. Internal logging format change.

eli5.text: Your assistant's internal logs now print log levels as clear uppercase words (like ERROR) instead of numbers, and every log entry includes a timestamp in the standard ISO format. Only the backend team building and maintaining your assistant is affected. If you ever inspect the logs, you'll see cleaner, uniformly formatted entries with readable level labels and timestamps that work with standard tools.
